claims.claim: Rigetti sits on a causal chain from superconducting quantum processors through fidelity/scaling and deployable systems to useful quantum-compute capacity; the 2026 Commerce agreement targets scaling bottlenecks while the Systems Delivery organization targets the processor-to-deployment bridge.
The principal successor bottleneck is commercialization: technical scale and government validation do not by themselves establish repeatable paid deployment economics.

risks.risk: Alternative quantum modalities or classical/AI substitutes can reduce the value captured by superconducting systems even if technical milestones are met.

contradictions.contradiction: Government/technical validation is strengthening while durable commercial demand remains early-stage.

unknowns.unknown: Repeatable system deployment economics and customer concentration remain unproven.

claims.claim: The strongest present challenge is conversion risk rather than lack of technical activity: 2025 revenue was only $7.1M while the company remained loss-making, so government funding and roadmap progress should not be treated as evidence of mature commercial demand.

risks.risk: High R&D intensity can consume capital before paid deployments scale; financing/dilution remains a relevant resilience risk.
Roadmap claims can overstate value capture if fidelity/scale milestones fail to convert into customer workloads and recurring revenue.

contradictions.contradiction: Technical/government validation is strengthening while the commercial revenue base remains early-stage.

unknowns.unknown: Current cash burn, gross margins and customer concentration require Alpha underwriting.
